title: Linear torsors and sections describing a reduction of structure group
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $n\geq1$, and $L=\operatorname{GL}_{n,S}$, the $S$-group of invertible $n\times n$ matrices, represented by $\operatorname{Spec}_S\mathcal O_S[x_{ab},d]/(d\det(x_{ab})-1)$. Let $H$ be a smooth affine finitely presented $S$-group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, pqf-def-affine-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], where group-object diagrams are interpreted over $S$. Suppose $i:H\hookrightarrow L$ is a closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion], its fppf right-coset quotient $Q=L/H$ is an affine $S$-scheme, and $L\to Q$ is a represented right $H$-torsor. Quotients mean sheafification of the orbit presheaf on the big fppf site [def-pc-fppf-site, def-weil-pbc-sheafification], and represented right torsors have the meaning of [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors]. For every $S$-scheme $T$, right $L_T$-torsors are equivalent to rank-$n$ finite locally free $\mathcal O_T$-modules [def-sc-finite-locally-free-sheaf]: $E$ corresponds to $E\times^{L_T}\mathcal O_T^n$, and a module $V$ corresponds to its frame scheme $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_T}(\mathcal O_T^n,V)$. For such a torsor $E$, the sheaf $E/H_T$ is represented by an affine $T$-scheme, and $E\to E/H_T$ is a right $H_T$-torsor. The functor $P\mapsto(E=P\times^{H_T}L_T,\sigma_P)$ is an equivalence between right $H_T$-torsors and pairs consisting of a right $L_T$-torsor $E$ and a section $\sigma:T\to E/H_T$; its inverse sends $(E,\sigma)$ to $E\times_{E/H_T,\sigma}T$. The contracted product is the sheaf quotient of $P\times_TL_T$ by $(p,l)\cdot h=(ph,i(h)^{-1}l)$, and $\sigma_P$ sends the class of $p$ to the right coset of $[p,1]$. All constructions and equivalences are natural under arbitrary base change $T'\to T$ of $S$-schemes. Consequently, let $G$ be an $S$-group scheme acting on $T$ by $a:G\times_ST\to T$, and let $\operatorname{pr}:G\times_ST\to T$ be the projection. A left $G$-action on a right $H_T$- or $L_T$-torsor $P\to T$ covering $a$ and commuting with the right action is the same as a torsor isomorphism $\phi:\operatorname{pr}^*P\simeq a^*P$ over $G\times_ST$ which is the identity after pulling back along the unit section $T\to G\times_ST$ and satisfies the cocycle law over $G\times_SG\times_ST$. Under the frame equivalence such data on $E$ correspond to $G$-linearizations of $V$, namely $\mathcal O$-linear isomorphisms $\operatorname{pr}^*V\simeq a^*V$ with the same unit and cocycle laws. Under the reduction equivalence an equivariant $H_T$-torsor $P$ corresponds to an equivariant $L_T$-torsor $E$ together with a section $\sigma$ that is invariant, meaning that the isomorphism $\operatorname{pr}^*(E/H_T)\simeq a^*(E/H_T)$ induced by $\phi$ sends $\operatorname{pr}^*\sigma$ to $a^*\sigma$; equivariant isomorphisms correspond to isomorphisms respecting these data.

source.place: WANTED locally; read https://sites.math.washington.edu/~jarod/papers/iwahori.pdf, Section 2, Claim 2, printed p.2, the equivalence between reductions and sections and translation between general linear torsors and vector bundles. Interpret contracted products on the fppf site, not pointwise orbit sets.

proof.text: Fix $T/S$. Use the big fppf site throughout. Every represented torsor $P\to T$ in [def-sfb-split-solvable-right-torsors] trivializes on the singleton fppf cover $P\to T$: its diagonal section pulls back to the trivialization $(p,h)\mapsto(p,ph)$, with inverse given by the stipulated torsor-square isomorphism. Fppf covers are fpqc by [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc], and representables are sheaves by [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-representable-descent]. Thus an identity of maps can be checked after these covers; compatible local maps and their inverses glue uniquely. For represented functors this gives scheme maps and scheme isomorphisms by [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful]. We use these facts only in the precise form just stated, including on base-changed covers.

Here is the affine descent operation used below. If an fppf sheaf $F$ over a scheme $B$ has affine representing schemes $X_i/B_i$ on an fppf cover $\{B_i\to B\}$, [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] supplies their canonical scheme descent datum. Encode it on $A=\coprod_i B_i$, $Z=\coprod_i X_i$ using [lem-trf-fppf-family-coproduct-descent-encoding]. The map $Z\to A$ is affine: an affine open of $A$ meets only finitely many disjoint open-and-closed components, and on each intersection its inverse image is affine; their finite disjoint union is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence]. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to obtain an effective singleton datum. The encoding gives effectivity of the original family datum, so the sheaf-descent statement represents $F$ by $X/B$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-fpqc-descend-affine] makes $X\to B$ affine, using the fpqc cover from step 1. This applies also to an empty base and its empty cover.

The matrix scheme $L_B$ for any $B/S$ is affine and finitely presented over $B$: on an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R\subset B$ its algebra is $R[x_{ab},d]/(d\det x-1)$, with finitely many generators and one relation; since $L_B\to B$ is affine, clause (3) of [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] makes it quasi-compact and separated, so it is of finite presentation and not only locally so. It is the determinant principal open in $\mathbf A_B^{n^2}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-section-vanishing-prime]. Affine space is smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth], and its open restriction is smooth by [lem-pc-open-immersion-smooth-composition]. It is flat by [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], and surjective since it has the identity section. Thus $L_B\to B$ is flat, surjective and finitely presented. The same three properties for $H_B\to B$ follow from the hypotheses, the identity section, [sbc-lem-smooth-criterion], and base-change stability in [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], applied to schemes. If a represented sheaf with right $L_B$- or $H_B$-action is locally equivariantly isomorphic to this group on an fppf cover, its structure morphism is flat and finitely presented by that node and surjective by [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. Its torsor square is an isomorphism: locally its inverse is $(x,y)\mapsto(x,x^{-1}y)$, and step 1 glues the inverse. It is therefore a represented right torsor in the definition used here.

proof.text: For a right $L_T$-torsor $E$, choose an fppf trivializing cover and sections $e_i$. On double overlaps let $g_{ij}$ be the unique matrix with $e_j=e_i g_{ij}$. The torsor square gives these as scheme maps. On triple overlaps, $g_{ik}=g_{ij}g_{jk}$. Glue the free modules $\mathcal O_{T_i}^n$ by identifying the vector $v$ in chart $j$ with $g_{ij}v$ in chart $i$. This is a quasi-coherent descent datum by the displayed matrix identity. Apply [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] with the fpqc cover of step 1: it gives a finite locally free module $V$ of rank $n$, and compatible linear maps descend uniquely. Its sheaf of sections on $U/T$ is the associated sheaf $E\times^{L_T}\mathcal O_T^n$: locally $[e_i l,v]\mapsto lv$ is a bijection, respecting $(el,v)\sim(e,lv)$, addition, and scalars. These local bijections agree because the same $g_{ij}$ occurs on both sides. The sheaf gluing axiom makes them global bijections. This both defines the associated module and identifies it with the descended one, without assuming pointwise orbit sets are sheaves.

source.place: Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent) and Tag 05B2 (lemma-finite-locally-free-descends); explicit matrix cocycle for Claim 2

proof.text: Conversely let $V$ be finite locally free of rank $n$. Define the frame sheaf on $U/T$ by $\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U^n,V|_U)$, with right action $f\cdot l=f\circ l$. It is an fppf sheaf: compatible module isomorphisms and their inverses descend by the full faithfulness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent], after step 1. A Zariski trivializing cover for $V$ identifies it with $L_{T_i}$, including the action. Step 2 represents this sheaf by an affine $T$-scheme; step 3 makes it a represented right torsor. The evaluation map $\operatorname{Fr}(V)\times^{L_T}\mathcal O_T^n\to V$ is $[f,v]\mapsto f(v)$, locally an isomorphism. For $E$ the map to the frames of its associated module sends $e$ to $(v\mapsto[e,v])$, and is locally the identity $L\to L$. Step 1 makes it a scheme isomorphism. These maps are natural: a linear isomorphism $b$ sends $f$ to $b\circ f$, while an equivariant torsor map $u$ sends $[e,v]$ to $[u(e),v]$. The evaluation maps commute with these formulas, so they give natural inverse equivalences of groupoids.

source.place: Tag 023T (proposition-fpqc-descent-quasi-coherent), full faithfulness; Claim 2, frame and evaluation constructions

proof.text: For the right $L_T$-torsor $E$ let $F=E/H_T$ be its fppf quotient sheaf. On a trivializing cover for $E$, it is $Q_{T_i}$. Indeed an orbit class there maps to its right coset in $L/H$; every coset locally lifts to $L$ because $L\to Q$ is the assumed torsor, and two lifts of the same coset differ by a unique $H$-element. These assertions identify the associated sheaves, even when a coset has no global lift. They also show that restricting the quotient sheaf to any further base change gives the same local quotient. Since $Q_{T_i}\to T_i$ is affine by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence], step 2 represents $F$ by an affine $T$-scheme $X$. The map $E\to X$ locally is $L\to Q$. Its pullback over a test scheme with a local lift $e$ to $E$ identifies with $H$ by $h\mapsto eh$. Such lifts exist fppf locally by the quotient construction and the assumed torsor. Step 3 proves that $E\to X$ is a represented right $H$-torsor. Thus $X$ is the asserted $E/H_T$.

source.place: Claim 2, affineness of the quotient; descent.tex Tags 02W5 and 0245, with the assumed represented torsor L to Q

proof.text: For a represented right $H_T$-torsor $P$, form the fppf sheaf quotient $E=(P\times_TL_T)/H_T$ with $(p,l)\cdot h=(ph,i(h)^{-1}l)$. Its right $L_T$-action is $[p,l]\cdot k=[p,lk]$; this is well defined because left multiplication by $i(h)^{-1}$ commutes with right multiplication by $k$. On a trivializing cover with section $p_i$, the formula $[p_i h,l]\mapsto i(h)l$ identifies it equivariantly with $L$, with inverse $l\mapsto[p_i,l]$. Apply [lem-galois-fpqc-affine-descent-effective] to the local affine $L$-model on the singleton cover $P\to T$, and [lem-trf-fppf-sheaf-representability-descent-data] as in step 2 to represent $E$; and step 3 makes it a represented $L_T$-torsor. Step 6 forms its affine quotient $E/H_T$. Locally define a section by $[p_i,1]H$. If $p_j=p_i h_{ij}$, then $[p_j,1]=[p_i,i(h_{ij})]$, so both cosets coincide. Step 1 glues the local maps to $\sigma_P:T\to E/H_T$. A torsor isomorphism $u:P\to P'$ induces $[p,l]\mapsto[u(p),l]$ and preserves these sections, by its displayed formula.

source.place: Alper--Halpern-Leistner--Heinloth, Section 2, Claim 2, printed p.2; explicit contracted-product construction using descent.tex Tags 0245 and 02W5

proof.text: Given $(E,\sigma)$, set $P=E\times_{E/H_T,\sigma}T$. It is an $H_T$-torsor: base change of step 6 gives its action and torsor square, and flatness, finite presentation and surjectivity survive base change by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality] and [lem-sfb-space-smooth-surjective-fppf-locality]. Its inclusion in $E$ induces $P\times^{H_T}L_T\to E$, $[p,l]\mapsto pl$. On a cover with a section $p$ of $P$ this is the identity between two trivial $L$-torsors, so step 1 proves it an isomorphism. It carries $\sigma_P$ to $\sigma$ since the image of $p$ in $E/H_T$ is $\sigma$. In the other direction $P\to(P\times^{H_T}L_T)\times_{(P\times^{H_T}L_T)/H_T,\sigma_P}T$, $p\mapsto([p,1],\mathrm{base}(p))$, is equivariant and locally is $H\to H$, hence an isomorphism by step 1. A map of pairs restricts to these fibre products, and extension sends it back to the original map by $[p,l]\mapsto pl$. Therefore the two comparisons are natural on arrows as well as on objects. This proves the reduction equivalence, rather than just a bijection on isomorphism classes.

source.place: Claim 2, inverse reduction by pullback of a section; spaces-descent.tex Tags 041V, 041W, 041Q

proof.text: All the comparisons above commute with an arbitrary $b:T'\to T$. For the associated module, pulling back the gluing data gives the same free modules and matrices $b^*g_{ij}$; uniqueness in [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] identifies the two descended modules. For frame schemes the comparison on $U/T'$ sends a frame of $b^*V|_U$ to that same frame of $V|_U$, so is a natural bijection and hence a scheme isomorphism by step 1. For the quotient and contracted product, the canonical maps are $[e]H\mapsto[e]H$ and $[p,l]\mapsto[p,l]$ on local representatives. On the pulled-back trivializing covers these are the identity maps of $Q$ and $L$ respectively; step 1 makes them isomorphisms globally. Fibre products commute with base change by their universal property. The same formulas show that each comparison preserves sections and arrows. Under two successive base changes both composites have the same formula on local representatives, hence agree. Thus the base-change identifications are coherent, not arbitrary choices of an isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 023T, uniqueness of descent; Claim 2, arbitrary base-change naturality, with explicit comparison formulas

proof.text: Write the torsor group over $S$ as $K$, equal to $H$ or $L$. A commuting left $G$-action $A$ on $P$ gives $\phi$ by $(g,t,p)\mapsto(g,t,A(g,p))$, where $p$ lies over $t$. Its inverse on the fibre over $(g,t)$ sends $q$ over $gt$ to $A(g^{-1},q)$. These are scheme maps because the action and inverse are scheme maps. Conversely $\phi:\operatorname{pr}^*P\simeq a^*P$ composed with the projection to $P$ gives $A:G\times_SP\to P$. The fact that $\phi$ is a $K$-torsor isomorphism says exactly $A(g,ph)=A(g,p)h$. Its unit law says $A(1,p)=p$; its cocycle law says $A(g_1,A(g_2,p))=A(g_1g_2,p)$. Thus these two constructions are inverse. They also identify a commuting equivariant torsor map with a map respecting $\phi$, by evaluating that same equation on $(g,p)$. No flatness or smoothness of the acting group $G$ is used.

source.place: Claim 2, commuting equivariant structures; unit and composition laws of the action groupoid

proof.text: Apply step 9 to the two maps $\operatorname{pr},a:G\times_ST\to T$. The frame equivalence sends a torsor isomorphism $\phi$ to the linear isomorphism $[e,v]\mapsto[\phi(e),v]$ of associated modules. Its inverse sends a frame $f$ to $b\circ f$ for a linear isomorphism $b$. These respect identities and composition by direct substitution, so the unit and cocycle equations in step 10 correspond exactly to the linearization equations. In the reduction equivalence, extending an $H$-torsor isomorphism gives $[p,l]\mapsto[\phi(p),l]$. The induced map of quotients therefore sends the local coset of $[p,1]$ to the local coset of $[\phi(p),1]$, proving the invariance equation for $\sigma_P$. Conversely, invariance of $\sigma$ makes $\phi$ restrict to an isomorphism between the two pullbacks of $P=\sigma^*E$; its unit and cocycle laws are the restrictions of those for $E$. Extension recovers $\phi$ since it agrees on every $[p,l]$. All comparisons in step 8 use these same formulas, hence commute with equivariant arrows. This proves both equivariant conclusions.
